sentences.text: 1. Nancy is meeting Paul Caruso, a web designer from a company called Glitch, to discuss creating a website for the concert.
Listen to the meeting and fill in the missing information in the spaces provided in the note sheet.
One has been done for you as an example.
You will have 30 seconds to study the task, At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Hello. Thanks for coming today, Paul.
I’m Nancy Chow.
We spoke on the phone.
Hi Nancy. Nice to meet you.
Right well, thanks for agreeing to design the website for our concert.
It’s my pleasure.
We're really looking for something quite simple at this stage.
OK, not a problem.
What's the name of this concert, by the way?
It’s called Music: A Night to Remember OK.
Music: A Night to Remember Right.
OK, what we'd normally have on a page like this is, like, the basic details that you want the public to know about.
Like, say, when the concert will take place.
OK, well, it'll be held on November the 24th.
November the 24th, this year, I presume.
Yeah, 2015. And the location?
Where will it be?
at the Central Theatre of the Hong Kong Cultural Centre.
OK. And the time?
When will it start?
It'll start at half past seven.
So from 7: thirty to 9: thirty pm.
Oh, another thing there is no interval!
If you could mention that on the website!
So no interval!
Ill make that clear.
And who can participate?
Well, young people between the ages of 13 and 18 can participate.
And they should either belong to a school group or an independent group.
So just groups?
No, no, solo participants are welcome too.
What types of performance are you looking for?
What kind of music are they allowed to perform?
Well, it can be jazz bands, rap groups, or even rock music.
OK. how about dance groups?
No, unfortunately, we won't be accepting dance groups just music groups.
And how do they apply?
Well, they should send in a video.
And the video should contain three things.
OK, three things.
Yeah, first it should contain a short video of the artists introducing themselves.
Second, it should have a video of a performance.
And what was the third thing?
Oh yeah, it should contain a video of them telling a funny story about what happened to them when they were performing.
Alright. How can the public get their tickets?
How can they contact you?
Have you got it set up online or Well, we've got four ways for people to buy tickets.
Right. First, they should be able to buy tickets online by clicking on a link or an icon in the shape of a shopping trolley.
OK, a link or an icon in the shape of a shopping trolley.
Secondly, they can call this number 749 -481 -61.
did you get it down?
correct? Yes, that’s correct.
Thirdly, they can send us an email at information at C -A -F dot org That’s O -R -G.
OK, the email address is information at C -A -F dot org Great, Plus, they can get tickets at the box office.
Alright, I think I have most of the important information for now.
Just a couple of questions about the look of the webpage.
OK, Let me show you some designs for a logo we've used for this type of event before.
We can adapt these a bit obviously.
So which of these four do you think would be the best for the show?
OK, let me see.
well, I don’t want the one with the brake dancers as I said, it’s a music concert.
So that one’s out.
um, I’m not sure about the one with the guitar.
It gives the impression that we're only looking for serious musicians and not singers.
Right, what about the other two?
Well, either of these would do but I think I'd go for this one.
Just because it’s a bunch of people together as opposed to just one girl.
OK and what would you like the background colour of this website to be?
Ooh, I'd like it to be red!
But it might be difficult to read the words if the background’s red.
Yeah, that’s true.
You know what, I think just a simple white background will do with black or maybe dark blue writing.
Great. rate. I can show you a temporary version of the website by next week.
And if you like it, we can meet again to discuss adding more information to the website.
Thank you very much, Paul!
I appreciate it!
You're welcome. See you next week.
